rich_summary: As the tenth day of the Kurukshetra war approaches, the Pandavas execute a plan centered on Sikhandin, whom Bhishma has vowed not to fight because of Sikhandin’s past birth as a woman. At dawn the Pandava army marches out with Sikhandin placed at the very front, protected by major heroes such as Arjuna and Bhima. Sanjaya describes both armies’ elaborate formations and the devastating clash that follows. The Pandavas initially press hard, causing heavy losses among the Kauravas. Enraged by the suffering of his army, Bhishma launches a ferocious counterattack, cutting down soldiers, elephants, and chariots in vast numbers and terrifying the battlefield. When Sikhandin finally confronts him, Bhishma refuses to fight, reaffirming his vow—setting the stage for the pivotal moment that will soon bring about the fall of the grandsire.

top_scenes.scene_text: At sunrise the Pandava army marches out with drums and white conches sounding, Sikhandin’s chariot leading while Arjuna and Bhima guard his wheels.
Bhishma stands blazing in the battlefield, his bow drawn in a perfect circle as showers of arrows fall around him and soldiers, elephants, and chariots collapse.
Sikhandin fires arrows into Bhishma’s chest while the grandsire calmly refuses to fight back, declaring he will never battle the one once born a woman.
